title: The falling hemoglobin in Chair 7
note: Fictional patient. Values are illustrative and follow the module’s KDIGO 2026 statements and grades; no doses are given. The unit’s protocol, formulary and the attending nephrologist decide every order.
intro:
You are the internal medicine resident on a month in the hospital hemodialysis (HD) unit. Mr. Rogelio Bautista, 47, a tricycle driver from Marikina, has dialyzed three times a week for eight months and is registered with PhilHealth. He transferred from another unit last week, and his anemia papers did not come with him. His younger brother has offered him a kidney, and the transplant workup has started.

Today’s monthly laboratory sheet shows hemoglobin (Hb) 8.4 g/dL and a mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 80 fL. He says he gets tired climbing to his second-floor room. He has no chest pain, and his blood pressure is stable. He is on no erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) and no iron. The charge nurse asks whether she should request two units of blood for today’s session “para mabilis.”

choices.text: Request two units for today’s session so he feels better by Wednesday.
choices.feedback: He is stable and breathless only on exertion. KDIGO 2026 bases transfusion on symptoms and signs, not an Hb number, and advises avoiding it in transplant candidates when possible (practice points). Each unit can sensitize him to human leukocyte antigens (HLA) and make his brother’s kidney harder to match.
choices.then: You cancel the request and send the first test set instead. He reports no black stools and no pain tablets.

choices.text: Send a complete blood count (CBC), reticulocytes, ferritin and transferrin saturation (TSAT) before any iron or blood; ask about black stools, pain tablets and past transfusions; no transfusion today.
choices.feedback: This is the KDIGO first test set (practice point), and it must be drawn before iron or blood changes the numbers. He is stable, and his brother’s offer makes him a transplant candidate, so transfusion is not needed today.

choices.text: Send a ferritin alone today, since it is the cheapest way to see his iron stores.
choices.feedback: Ferritin is also an acute-phase protein, so it can look adequate while the marrow is starved. Every KDIGO iron threshold pairs it with TSAT, and a reticulocyte count tells you whether the marrow is responding.
choices.then: You add TSAT and a reticulocyte count to the same sample. He reports no black stools and no pain tablets.

choices.text: Start an ESA today and send the iron studies next week.
choices.feedback: An ESA cannot build red cells without iron. KDIGO 2026 asks you to address every correctable cause, including iron deficiency, before an ESA (practice point).
choices.then: You hold the ESA and send the first test set today. He reports no black stools and no pain tablets.

n2.scene: The results are back: ferritin 310 ng/mL, TSAT 18%, reticulocyte production index (RPI) 0.9. There is no sign of infection, and the history finds no bleeding.

choices.text: No iron: a ferritin above 300 ng/mL means his stores are full.
choices.feedback: The 300 ng/mL cut point belongs to patients not on dialysis. In HD, KDIGO 2026 suggests starting iron when ferritin is ≤500 ng/mL and TSAT ≤30% (2D). He meets it.
choices.then: The attending corrects the threshold, and an intravenous iron course starts at dialysis.

choices.text: Oral ferrous sulfate for three months, then recheck.
choices.feedback: Iron is right, but the route is not. KDIGO 2026 suggests intravenous rather than oral iron when starting in HD (2D). Hepcidin limits gut absorption, and he is already in the unit three times a week.
choices.then: The attending switches the plan to intravenous iron at dialysis.

choices.text: Intravenous iron at dialysis, given where a reaction can be managed, with the dose from the unit formulary.
choices.feedback: Ferritin ≤500 ng/mL with TSAT ≤30% meets the KDIGO 2026 HD threshold, and intravenous is the suggested route (both 2D). Name the grade: these are weak suggestions on very low certainty evidence, sensible boundaries rather than proof.

n3.scene: After the iron course, his Hb is 9.0 g/dL. He is still tired, and his wife asks about the “vitamin for blood” the other patients get.
n3.prompt: What do you propose to the attending?

choices.text: Start an ESA and aim for an Hb of 13 g/dL, so he finally feels normal.
choices.feedback: CHOIR and TREAT tested higher targets. Aiming high brought more cardiovascular events or strokes, with little gain in how patients felt. KDIGO 2026 recommends keeping Hb below 11.5 g/dL in adults on an ESA (1D).
choices.then: The attending writes the order with an Hb ceiling below 11.5 g/dL instead.

choices.text: Start an ESA now and write the ceiling in the order: keep Hb below 11.5 g/dL.
choices.feedback: On dialysis, KDIGO 2026 suggests starting an ESA when Hb is at or below 9.0 to 10.0 g/dL (2D), and the ceiling is its one strong recommendation (1D). The aim is fewer symptoms and fewer transfusions, not a normal Hb.

choices.text: A hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor (HIF-PHI) tablet instead, so he avoids injections.
choices.feedback: KDIGO 2026 suggests an ESA rather than a HIF-PHI as first-line treatment (2D). Longer experience with HIF-PHIs is limited, and he is in the unit three times a week, where injections are easy.
choices.then: The attending starts an ESA at dialysis, with a ceiling below 11.5 g/dL.

vitals.symptom: No thrill or bruit in left arm fistula

n4.scene: The nurse calls you before the session: there is no thrill and no bruit over his left arm fistula. Today’s pre-dialysis Hb is 11.9 g/dL.

choices.text: Call the attending now, suspend the ESA, and arrange urgent vascular access assessment per the unit protocol.
choices.feedback: KDIGO 2026 advises suspending an ESA during access thrombosis (practice point), and his Hb is already above the 11.5 g/dL ceiling. A clotted fistula is time-sensitive, and the attending decides how he dialyzes today.

choices.text: Lower the ESA dose a little and review at next month’s labs.
choices.feedback: Lowering is the right direction for an Hb above the ceiling. But the practice point for access thrombosis is to suspend the ESA, and the fistula needs urgent attention today, not next month.
choices.then: The attending, told at rounds, suspends the ESA and calls the access team.

choices.text: Keep the ESA as is; his Hb is finally doing well.
choices.feedback: An Hb of 11.9 g/dL is above the ceiling, not a success. In TREAT, the higher target nearly doubled strokes. With a fresh thrombosis, the ESA should be suspended.
choices.then: The charge nurse asks you to check with the attending, who suspends the ESA and calls the access team.

n5.scene: The fistula could not be saved. He now dialyzes through a tunneled catheter while a new fistula matures. The ESA was restarted, but his Hb has fallen to 8.7 g/dL despite two dose increases. Ferritin is 780 ng/mL and TSAT 22%. He mentions chills in the evenings.

choices.text: Raise the ESA dose again until the Hb responds.
choices.feedback: This is ESA hyporesponsiveness. In the trials, patients who needed the most ESA did worst. KDIGO 2026 asks you to find and treat the cause first (practice point).
choices.then: The attending stops the escalation and asks you to work up the cause, starting with the catheter.

choices.text: Treat it as hyporesponsiveness: tell the attending today, look for infection starting with the catheter, then blood loss, hyperparathyroidism, dialysis adequacy and missed sessions; hold iron for now.
choices.feedback: Infection and inflammation raise hepcidin and blunt the marrow, and the catheter is the likely source. KDIGO 2026 makes it reasonable to withhold routine iron with ferritin above 700 ng/mL, and to consider pausing iron during a systemic infection (practice points).

choices.text: Give more intravenous iron, since TSAT is still below 30%.
choices.feedback: TSAT is low because inflammation is locking iron away, not because stores are empty. With ferritin above 700 ng/mL and possible infection, the practice points favor holding iron while you find the cause.
choices.then: The attending holds the iron and asks for a catheter infection workup.

end.title: Month 12
end.text: Blood cultures confirmed a catheter infection, treated by the attending’s plan. Over the next months his Hb rose without further ESA increases. He was never transfused, and his brother’s workup continues. The unit supplies his ESA and iron under the PhilHealth hemodialysis package; you confirmed what the unit actually provides before writing the plan.

debrief:
What this case teaches

  • Draw the first test set before iron or blood: CBC, reticulocytes, ferritin and TSAT, read together.
  • Know which threshold applies. In HD, start iron at ferritin ≤500 ng/mL and TSAT ≤30%, intravenously (2D); 300 ng/mL is the cut point off dialysis.
  • Use an ESA to spare symptoms and transfusions, not to reach normal. Keep adult Hb below 11.5 g/dL (1D), and suspend the ESA during access thrombosis.
  • A poor response is a question, not a dose. Look for infection, blood loss, hyperparathyroidism and missed dialysis; withhold routine iron above a ferritin of 700 ng/mL.
  • Ask about transplant plans before every unit of blood.

See Work-up, Iron, ESA and HIF-PHI and Transfusion.
